Caroline, Kimberly — quick technical clarity from infra: 

- For Redwood Private deployed in a customer VPC in eu-west-1, the data plane (model inputs, outputs, KV cache) and host-local logs remain in customer subnets in eu-west-1. The control plane is configurable; for BrightLeaf we recommend the "private control plane" option which keeps all management communication over the established peering/privatelink and does not inject metrics into other regions.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via the cloud provider KMS or via on-prem HSM connector. With BYOK, the cryptographic key material remains in your KMS/HSM and Redwood components request decryption via API calls that honor your key policies. We can provide an HSM attestation excerpt and an example key rotation schedule.
- Telemetry: runtime aggregated telemetry is opt-in for hosted monitoring. For Private deployments we can disable telemetry to external endpoints entirely; operational metrics can be delivered into your monitoring stack in-region.

Attaching the updated network diagram and a draft evidence matrix to speed review. I redacted internal employee names in the diagram.

Attachments: network_diagram_v2.pdf (diagram), evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix)

—Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference
